signals.name: Silver
signals.label: Holds ~$59.5 on a two-day bounce, still rate-hostage
signals.detail: Silver ~$59.5 (Wed 22 Jul), +~1.1% on top of Tue's ~4%; ~50% below Jan record
signals.takeaway: The single most important line item for this book and its highest-beta pain. Silver rose ~1.1% Wednesday 22 July to ~$59.4-59.6/oz, extending Tuesday's ~4% rip, as the war/oil premium (Brent >$94) fed safe-haven and inflation-hedge demand and the S&P held a record. It has retraced most of last week's slide but remains ~50% below January's ~$121 record, and the driver is the geopolitical/inflation premium, not a real-rates thaw: the 28-29 Jul FOMC is ~80% hold with a live September-hike tail. The structural deficit thesis holds (Silver Institute 2026 deficit; JPMorgan ~$81 average), but the metal is trading as a rate/geopolitical asset, not a clean hedge. Treat the bounce as a spot to right-size leverage into next week's FOMC; $58 is the near-term line to hold above, a Hormuz de-escalation the downside risk.

signals.name: SPDR Gold Shares
signals.label: Rebounds ~1.8% to ~$4,150 with a CB floor
signals.detail: Gold ~$4,152 (+~1.8% Wed 22 Jul); ~28% below Jan record, +~22% YoY
signals.takeaway: Gold rose ~1.8% Wednesday 22 July to ~$4,151/oz, from ~$4,054 the prior session, riding the risk/safe-haven bid as the Iran war premium built. It has reclaimed the $4,000 shelf it defended near multi-month lows and is up ~22% YoY, but remains ~28% below its 29 Jan record (~$5,595). Miners lag bullion on cost inflation (GDX ~$74, -14% YTD). The rates channel is still the dominant driver — a firm-ish dollar (DXY ~101) and higher-for-longer Fed cap the metal — so this is a bounce within a correction, not yet a trend change. The structural floor is real: central-bank buying (PBoC multi-month streak) and record YTD gold-fund inflows (+$75bn) underpin it. A clean reclaim of the spring highs signals the miners' washout is done; a fade back to $4,000 keeps them on watch. The 28-29 July FOMC is the swing.

signals.name: Semiconductors / AI-capex
signals.label: Sharp memory-led rebound after the unwind
signals.detail: Micron +12%, Sandisk +14%, AMD +8% Tue; megacap earnings the test
signals.takeaway: After being the market's biggest loser (SOX -11% on the month, SMH ~20% off the 6/22 peak on AI-capex-peak fears), semis staged a violent reversal Tuesday 21 July: Micron +12%, Sandisk +14% on memory strength and AMD +8% extending its Microsoft AI-deal gains, lifting the Nasdaq +1.29% and snapping a three-day losing streak. Breadth firmed with it (S&P >200-DMA back to ~68.6%, highest since Feb) and ~88% of the ~66 S&P reporters beat EPS. But the bounce is earnings-contingent: major megacap AI results this week will confirm or break the capex story, and Burry's chip shorts remain the structural counter-view. The AI-capex engine (>$400B 2026 hyperscaler capex) is the 12m floor; the rebound is a relief, not yet a confirmed all-clear.

signals.name: Energy Select Sector
signals.label: War premium; the leading sector
signals.detail: WTI ~$79-82 / Brent ~$84, +13% in 5 days on the Iran war
signals.takeaway: The energy thesis flipped hard. The June US-Iran ceasefire collapsed into a shooting war (a sixth night of US airstrikes by 17 July, a naval blockade throttling the Strait of Hormuz to ~7 vessels/day), driving Brent to ~$84 and WTI to ~$79-82, up ~13% in five days. Energy is now the LEADING S&P sector and the destination for money fleeing the semis unwind, joined by financials and industrials. Republican members had been accumulating traditional energy on the power-demand thesis; the war premium now pays that bet. But it is geopolitics-driven — a ceasefire or Hormuz de-escalation deflates it fast, as it did in June — so it is a near-term momentum/hedge long, not a buy-and-hold.

signals.name: MP Materials / rare earths
signals.label: Lynas Q4 MISS hits the ex-China basket
signals.detail: LYC.AX 5-month low on Q4 sales A$289m vs ~A$391m consensus; IEA warns $6.5T at risk
signals.takeaway: The sell-the-news risk flagged yesterday materialized: Lynas — the largest ex-China separator — fell to a five-month low after Q4 (to 30 June) sales of A$288.9m (+9% y/y) badly missed the ~A$391m consensus, with rare-earth sales VOLUMES declining, after a ~63% three-month run. That is a near-term negative read-through for the whole ex-China watchlist (MP, USAR, UUUU, REMX) on volume/pricing softness. But the strategic supply-security thesis is intact and, if anything, escalating: the IEA warned (16 Jul) that full China export curbs could jeopardize $6.5T of downstream production, a 1 Jul reporting mechanism signals tighter enforcement, and a suspension of expanded controls expires 10 Nov — a hard catalyst date. China still controls ~70% of mining and ~90% of processing/magnets, so each escalation raises the strategic value of Western names with a US-government financing floor (Energy Fuels' $725M OSC commitment, CEO insider buy). Treat basket weakness as watch-and-wait, not an automatic add; 6680.HK (JL MAG) is the relatively insulated Chinese-incumbent counter-bet.

signals.name: Inflation / Fed
signals.label: Soft CPI vs a hawkish, split Fed into 28-29 Jul
signals.detail: July FOMC ~80% hold at 3.50-3.75%; committee evenly split, live Sept-hike tail
signals.takeaway: June CPI resolved soft (headline -0.4% m/m to +3.5% y/y as energy fell 5.7%; core flat, +2.6% y/y) — the feared hot-core did not materialize — but the disinflation win is being clouded by July's oil spike (Brent >$94) doing the Fed's hawkish work. Markets price the 28-29 July FOMC at ~80% hold (3.50-3.75%); the 17 June minutes showed officials evenly split, roughly half favoring holds/cuts and half a hike before year-end, and the oil impulse keeps a September-hike tail alive. Chair Warsh reiterates the 2% target 'is not yet met'. That is why metals stay capped despite soft data — real rates and the dollar (DXY ~101) hold firm, 10Y ~4.63%. The FOMC is the next catalyst; a dovish 29 July surprise or an Iran de-escalation that deflates oil would be the cleanest metals/HK-tech positive.

signals.name: Tencent
signals.label: National-team bid + buyback + HK-tech AI rotation
signals.detail: HSI +2% Mon on state-fund buying; Tencent +3.5%, buyback ongoing
signals.takeaway: China tech is one of the few risk pockets with an explicit policy put this week. HK stocks rallied ~2% Monday 20 July (HS Tech +2.8%) as Beijing moved to shore up markets: the CSRC convened market participants and two state-backed funds disclosed fresh equity purchases. Tencent rose ~3.5%, Xiaomi and Alibaba +3%+, and foundries SMIC/Hua Hong +3%+ — China chips trading on domestic AI demand, decoupled from the prior week's US SOX rout. Underneath, Tencent's own buyback continues (~1.59M shares 6-9 July under the ~912M-share 10% mandate) alongside Xiaomi's (3.9M shares, HK$100.7M, 15 July) and Kuaishou's. The near-mechanical corporate bid plus the national-team put underpin the book's Tencent/HK-tech sleeve, though the PBoC's 14th straight LPR hold (3.00%/3.50%) shifts the burden to fiscal follow-through at the late-July Politburo.

signals.name: Amazon / smart-money consensus
signals.label: The most-bought hedge-fund name
signals.detail: Tepper near-doubled it; top-3 for Bridgewater & Ackman (Q1 13F)
signals.takeaway: Amazon is the tightest smart-money consensus long in the Q1 2026 13F data — the most-bought hedge-fund name of the quarter. David Tepper (Appaloosa) nearly doubled it to his top position (~15%), it sits top-3 for Bridgewater and top-2 (~17%) for Ackman's Pershing Square. The broader AI-infrastructure consensus (NVDA, TSM added by Bridgewater/Tiger/Soros/Tepper; AVGO by Druckenmiller/Bridgewater/Tiger) still dominates the tape — but that same crowded semis complex is exactly what just unwound (SMH -9%), and 13F data is a ~3.5-month-stale 31 March snapshot. A consensus worth respecting for direction, not chasing at the top; Q2 13Fs land 14 August.

congress.rationale: The Pennsylvania Republican made a series of five partial NVIDIA sales between 31 March and 2 July 2026, trimming the AI bellwether.
congress.deepDive: Meuser's staggered NVDA disposals drew fresh scrutiny in a 14 July Foreign Policy Journal piece flagging members trading semiconductors in sectors Congress can regulate (export controls, CHIPS oversight). The sells coincide with the semiconductor unwind (SOX -11% on the month) and Burry's chip shorts — whether prescient or coincidental, it is a notable trim of the market's most-owned AI name by a member with policy exposure.

congress.rationale: The California Democrat disclosed a large partial sale of Qualcomm, a chip name in a sector under active congressional regulation.
congress.deepDive: Jacobs' seven-figure QCOM disposal was one of the trades highlighted in the 14 July reform-bill coverage on members trading regulated-sector semiconductors. It lands amid the AI-capex-doubt correction that hit the broader chip complex, and reads as de-risking a single large-cap position rather than a sector-wide call.

congress.rationale: The Texas Republican reduced Atlas Energy Solutions (frac sand / energy services) exposure.
congress.deepDive: Roy's AESI sale trims a traditional-energy services name just before the US-Iran war re-armed the oil-price premium (WTI ~$82) — timing that, in hindsight, cut exposure ahead of the energy sector becoming the market's leader. A modest-sized, sector-specific disposal from a fiscal-hawk member.

congress.rationale: The Alabama Republican (now running for governor) sold Mastercard as part of a broad multi-name portfolio trim disclosed 16 July.
congress.deepDive: Tuberville disclosed a cluster of small sells (MA, PFE, NEE, DUK) transacted 8 June and filed mid-July, spanning payments, pharma and utilities. The breadth across unrelated sectors reads as an account-level rebalancing or liquidation rather than any single sector view.

congress.deepDive: Pfizer has been a chronic underperformer; the small sell fits the broader Tuberville portfolio cleanup rather than a fresh healthcare call. Filed 16 July under STOCK Act reporting.

congress.rationale: Trimming NextEra Energy (utility / renewables) in the same 8 June batch.
congress.deepDive: NEE and DUK sells trim rate-sensitive utility exposure just as the 10Y hovered ~4.56% and the Fed leaned hold-or-hike — consistent with reducing bond-proxy names, though the small size argues for routine rebalancing.

congress.rationale: Duke Energy sale completing the utility de-risking in the 8 June batch.
congress.deepDive: The second utility disposal alongside NEE; together they lighten interest-rate-sensitive holdings into a higher-for-longer regime. Disclosed 16 July.

congress.rationale: Disclosed 23 June — a sizable bet on an Intel foundry/turnaround, a contrarian position now echoed by Druckenmiller's new stake.
congress.deepDive: Pelosi's (via spouse) INTC purchase is a classic contrarian, policy-adjacent bet: Intel sits at the center of US semiconductor-reshoring and CHIPS support, and the buy now overlaps with Druckenmiller's fresh Q1 Intel position — a rare Congress/super-investor turnaround consensus. The AI/foundry angle makes it one of the more decision-relevant congressional trades this window.

congress.rationale: A seven-figure add to Uber, extending the household's mega-cap mobility/tech tilt.
congress.deepDive: The largest single congressional purchase in the window, continuing Pelosi's well-tracked mega-cap growth bias. Uber sits outside the semis unwind and benefits from the autonomous/mobility and consumer-resilience themes; the size makes it a closely watched signal for retail copy-traders.

congress.rationale: The Pennsylvania Republican sold Medicaid-exposed health insurers (Centene, UnitedHealth, Elevance, CVS) shortly before voting for Medicaid cuts, per a June-2026 disclosure — one of the window's most scrutinized conflict-of-interest trades.
congress.deepDive: Bresnahan disclosed a cluster of health-sector disposals transacted mid-May and reported in June, spanning Medicaid/managed-care names right before a vote on legislation cutting Medicaid — the kind of policy-adjacent timing that keeps STOCK Act reform in the headlines. Whether foresight or coincidence, it trimmed exposure to insurers most exposed to the funding change. A notable, well-reported fresh item added for member variety and decision relevance.

congress.rationale: The New Jersey Democrat sold Agree Realty (a net-lease REIT), disclosed 7 July 2026 — trimming a rate-sensitive bond-proxy into a higher-for-longer regime.
congress.deepDive: Gottheimer is an active, closely-tracked filer; the ADC sale lightens a net-lease REIT whose valuation is pressured by the 10Y holding ~4.63% and a Fed that is on hold-or-hike. A small, sector-consistent disposal rather than a broad market call, kept for member variety alongside the fresher July filings.

congress.deepDive: A modest bank disposal as the yield curve normalized and big-bank Q2 results approached mid-July; reads as routine rebalancing/profit-taking rather than a financials-sector call. Kept for member variety alongside the fresher July trades.

superInvestors.name: Scion Asset Management
superInvestors.rationale: Michael Burry disclosed a direct short on Micron (entry ~$1,051.87) on 2 July 2026, on top of fresh 30 June shorts against NVIDIA, Applied Materials and the iShares Semiconductor ETF, arguing AI chips face a ~30% correction.
superInvestors.deepDive: Having deregistered as an SEC adviser in late 2025, Burry no longer files 13Fs and now discloses via Substack — so these are his freshest, most public bets, and they are working: SMH is down ~9% over four weeks. He calls Micron 'cyclical like no other' and the trade is the cleanest smart-money expression of the AI-capex-peak thesis now playing out in the tape.

superInvestors.name: Berkshire Hathaway
superInvestors.rationale: In Greg Abel's first quarter running the book, Berkshire roughly tripled its Alphabet position — a rare, sizeable AI/search conviction add from Omaha.
superInvestors.deepDive: The GOOGL add is the marquee move of Berkshire's Q1 2026 13F (filed ~15 May) and pointedly diverges from Ackman and Druckenmiller, who both exited Alphabet the same quarter — the sharpest smart-money split of the quarter. Abel simultaneously slimmed the portfolio from ~40 to ~26 names ($274B→$263B), so the GOOGL conviction stands out against broad housecleaning.

superInvestors.name: Berkshire Hathaway
superInvestors.rationale: Berkshire's largest new buy of Q1 2026 — a ~$2.6B Delta Air Lines stake, re-entering airlines it had famously exited in 2020.
superInvestors.deepDive: A notable reversal of Buffett's post-Covid 'airlines are a mistake' stance, executed under Abel. The re-entry into a cyclical, capital-intensive carrier signals a value/reopening tilt and is one of the quarter's most-watched new positions.

superInvestors.name: Berkshire Hathaway
superInvestors.rationale: Berkshire fully exited Amazon (among 16 total exits including UNH, V, MA, DPZ) as Abel cut the roster from ~40 to ~26 names.
superInvestors.deepDive: The AMZN exit is striking because Amazon is simultaneously the single most-bought name across the rest of the super-investor cohort (Tepper doubled it, Ackman/Bridgewater/Tiger top-weighted). Berkshire selling the consensus long while raising cash underscores a valuation-discipline stance divergent from the AI-mega-cap crowd.

superInvestors.name: Pershing Square
superInvestors.rationale: Bill Ackman opened a big new Microsoft stake, buying into Q1 weakness in the mega-cap software leader.
superInvestors.deepDive: Ackman's concentrated ~11-name, ~$13.7B book added MSFT as a new anchor while he near-fully exited Alphabet (−~95%) and trimmed BN/UBER/QSR/META. The MSFT buy is a quality-compounder tilt into the AI-platform layer rather than the semis hardware that just unwound.

superInvestors.name: Pershing Square
superInvestors.rationale: Ackman cut Alphabet by ~95%, a near-complete exit — the opposite side of Berkshire's tripling.
superInvestors.deepDive: The Ackman (and Druckenmiller) GOOGL exits versus Berkshire's big add frame the quarter's clearest disagreement on a single mega-cap. For a book as concentrated as Pershing's, a 95% cut is a decisive negative verdict on Alphabet's risk/reward.

superInvestors.name: Appaloosa
superInvestors.rationale: David Tepper roughly doubled Amazon to his largest position, cementing it as the cohort's broadest consensus long.
superInvestors.deepDive: Tepper's AMZN doubling — alongside adds to MU (+11%, ~$562M, #2 holding) and TSM (+18%) and a new SanDisk stake — is an aggressive AI-infrastructure and memory bet, even as he trimmed Alibaba for a fifth straight quarter. It is the mirror image of Berkshire's AMZN exit.

superInvestors.name: Appaloosa
superInvestors.rationale: Tepper added ~11% to Micron, making it his #2 position on a memory-supercycle bet — directly opposite Burry's fresh MU short.
superInvestors.deepDive: The MU long (Tepper, Druckenmiller, Bridgewater) versus Burry's July short is the market's sharpest single-name battle: the AI-memory-demand bulls against the cyclical-peak bear. With SMH down ~9%, the short has the near-term edge, but the 13F longs are a 31 March snapshot.

superInvestors.name: Duquesne
superInvestors.rationale: Stanley Druckenmiller opened a new Broadcom stake (plus SNDK, TWLO, NET, INTC), doubling his tech weight to ~18.4% — while fully exiting Alphabet.
superInvestors.deepDive: Druckenmiller's aggressive tech/semis tilt (AVGO, SNDK, added MU/STX) plus new Intel and LatAm calls (EWZ/YPF) is a high-conviction AI-and-emerging-markets barbell. The GOOGL exit aligns him with Ackman against Berkshire; the memory/storage adds echo Tepper.

superInvestors.name: Soros Fund Management
superInvestors.rationale: Soros raised its NVIDIA stake ~61%, adding to the AI anchor even as some in Congress (Meuser) trimmed it.
superInvestors.deepDive: The Soros NVDA add fits the pervasive institutional AI-chip conviction across Bridgewater and Tiger (both top-weighted NVDA). That same crowded complex is exactly what unwound in July — a reminder that 13F longs are stale by ~3.5 months and the Q2 filings (due 14 Aug) will show whether conviction survived the semis rout.

superInvestors.name: Tiger Global
superInvestors.rationale: Chase Coleman kept a highly concentrated AI/tech book (GOOGL, NVDA, AMZN, TSM, META ~48% of assets).
superInvestors.deepDive: Tiger's top-five concentration in mega-cap AI is among the purest expressions of the consensus trade; it held GOOGL even as Ackman/Druckenmiller exited — another data point in the Alphabet disagreement. Concentration this high amplifies both the AI upside and the drawdown risk from the semis unwind.

superInvestors.name: Gates Foundation Trust
superInvestors.rationale: The Gates Foundation's low-turnover ~$31.7B book stayed anchored in Berkshire (25.8%), Microsoft, Waste Management, Canadian National and Caterpillar.
superInvestors.deepDive: A deliberately stable, quality-industrial portfolio that contrasts with the hedge-fund AI churn — useful as a defensive, low-beta benchmark. Minimal Q1 turnover means it offers signal by what it steadfastly holds rather than by fresh trades.

insiders.insider: Ross R. Bhappu (with dir. Bruce D. Hansen)
insiders.rationale: Open-market cluster buying by Energy Fuels’ top brass: CEO Bhappu bought 74,000 shares at $13.08 on 7 Jul (to 256,583 direct) and director Hansen 4,000 at $12.695 on 8 Jul (to 313,844). Both Form 4s accepted by SEC EDGAR 9 Jul 2026.
insiders.deepDive: Rare genuine open-market buys (not option exercises) in the portfolio’s uranium/rare-earth name — management conviction at the $12.70-13.08 zone makes that band an insider-validated reference level. It is also the only confirmed insider BUYING across the portfolio’s mining names this month, against heavy AI-complex insider selling (Arista founder -$54.2M, CoreWeave CEO -$24.8M in 14-16 Jul trades) — a striking sector contrast.

insiders.rationale: Xiaomi repurchased 1.9M Class B shares for HK$50.0M on 22 July 2026 — the most recent tranche in the window — after buying 3.9M shares for HK$100.7M on 15 July (HKEX filings), continuing its multi-tranche buyback program alongside a strong June EV-delivery print (+36% to 34,738 units).
insiders.deepDive: An issuer repurchase signals management's capital-allocation confidence rather than a single insider's personal bet, and Xiaomi's buyback runs in parallel with Tencent's HK program. The near-daily cadence into late July reinforces a company backing its own equity as the EV ramp (YU7 SUV, third straight 30k+ delivery month) diversifies the story beyond handsets/IoT. The corporate bid offers downside support for the holding through tech-sector volatility, though Xiaomi remains a high-beta HK-tech name that swings with the HSTECH tape (and still lags ~-34% YTD, offering relative catch-up if the rally broadens).

insiders.rationale: Tencent repurchased ~1,592,600 shares across 6-9 July 2026 (HK$204.8M on 6 July, HK$12.7M on 8 July and HK$500.7M on 9 July), extending a near-daily buyback streak under the ~912M-share (10%) mandate approved at the 13 May 2026 AGM. Separately, a Tencent unit sold up to ~US$1.55B of Kuaishou in a block trade (filed ~6 July) — a portfolio realization, distinct from the buyback.
insiders.deepDive: Company buybacks are a strong corporate-level conviction signal, and Tencent runs one of the largest repurchase programs in Hong Kong. The relentless daily cadence into July reflects a commitment to shrinking the share count and offsetting dilution from share-based compensation, bullish for holders as the stock coincided with an HK-tech rebound on AI catalysts (HSTECH +300pts, Alibaba ~+11%) and heavy southbound buying into Tencent (+HK$2.32B on 6 July). The parallel Kuaishou block sale is a capital-recycling move, not a signal on Tencent itself. Unlike a director's open-market buy, an issuer repurchase signals management's capital-allocation confidence rather than a single insider's personal bet. As of early July the program had run ~32 consecutive trading days for ~34.5M shares cumulatively under the 13-May mandate (up to ~912M sh / 10%) — a near-mechanical corporate bid underpinning the stock through the HK-tech rebound.

insiders.role: CEO & Executive Director, Mapletree Logistics Trust Mgmt
insiders.rationale: Mapletree Logistics Trust's CEO made an open-market purchase of ~100,000 units at ~S$1.91 in early July 2026, boosting her personal holding by ~73% — a genuine director conviction buy in the S-REIT sleeve as the trust trades near multi-year lows on the higher-for-longer rate backdrop (fresh SGX director-interest change this run).
insiders.deepDive: Unlike an issuer buyback, a CEO's own-account open-market purchase is a direct personal-conviction signal, and a ~73% boost to her stake is meaningful. It lands with MLT under pressure from higher-for-longer rates and a weak logistics-rent cycle in China/HK — the CEO stepping in near the lows is an insider-validated reference level for the industrial-S-REIT complex the book holds (MapletreePACT, Keppel REIT peers). Rate relief from a dovish FOMC pivot is the swing factor; until then the DPU/leverage trajectory caps upside. One of the few fresh, dated SGX director buys verifiable this run against limited SGXNet full-text access.

insiders.rationale: Capital Group crossed above the 5% substantial-shareholder threshold in Singtel, filing a notice showing a total 837,947,249 shares (5.1%) at an average ~S$4.67 — a large institutional accumulation in one of the portfolio's SGX holdings (latest available substantial-shareholder move on the SGX list).
insiders.deepDive: A global institution crossing 5% in Singtel is a meaningful vote of confidence in the telco's ongoing capital-return and asset-recycling story as the STI printed record highs into mid-July. Substantial-shareholder notices are a cleaner institutional signal than director trades and are among the few dated SGX disclosures verifiable this run. The one fresh SGX buyback that surfaced this run was Yangzijiang Maritime Development Ltd — a related but distinct listing from the shipbuilder — repurchasing 1.43M shares for ~S$0.84M across 25-26 June 2026 under an inaugural buyback mandate (recorded here as context; ticker not asserted to avoid mislabeling). No within-window substantial-shareholder or director-interest change was verifiable for DBS, F&N, VICOM, CityDev, UOL, Wing Tai, Yanlord, Ho Bee, Seatrium, CapLandChinaTr, Keppel REIT or Mapletree PACT this run — SGXNet full-text access was limited, so treat that list as unconfirmed rather than empty.

insiders.role: EVP & Chief Sustainability and Development Officer
insiders.rationale: Newmont's EVP sold 3,000 shares (~$277K) at $92.38 on 1 July 2026 (filed 6 July) under a Rule 10b5-1 plan dated 17 December 2025, leaving 43,315 shares — routine, pre-scheduled selling at the world's largest gold miner (a top GDX holding).
insiders.deepDive: This is a scheduled 10b5-1 disposal rather than a discretionary conviction sell, so the signal is muted — executives routinely diversify into strength, and gold near $4,150 makes profit-taking unremarkable. As the largest US-filing gold producer and a core GDX constituent, Newmont insider activity is a useful read on miner sentiment, and the absence of any open-market buying alongside these sales is consistent with a sector that already re-rated hard before June's pullback. Most large GDX/SILJ miners are Canadian foreign private issuers reporting on SEDI rather than US Form 4, so Newmont is one of the few that surfaces in SEC filings.

insiders.rationale: Hecla Mining's General Counsel had ~23,973 shares withheld for tax on RSUs that vested 22 June 2026, with the CFO seeing similar RSU vesting/withholding — equity-compensation events, not open-market buying or selling, at a core silver miner (SILJ/GDX).
insiders.deepDive: These are routine compensation/tax-withholding transactions rather than directional trades, so the signal value is low, but they are among the few recent US Form 4 filings in the largely-Canadian silver-miner universe. Hecla is the largest US primary silver producer and a SILJ constituent, making its filings a window into silver-complex insider behavior that SEDI-reporting peers otherwise hide. No open-market buying accompanied the vesting, consistent with insiders neither chasing nor fading the post-crash silver bounce.

insiders.rationale: Coeur Mining's EVP Exploration made a small open-market purchase of 635 shares (~$10.8K) at $16.95 on 12 June 2026 — the most recent verified Coeur insider transaction, a modest genuine-conviction buy at a US-domiciled silver/gold producer (latest available).
insiders.deepDive: Coeur is one of the few US-domiciled precious-metals miners that files Form 4, making it a window into silver-complex insider sentiment that the largely-Canadian SILJ/SLVP universe hides on SEDI. A small EVP open-market purchase is a modest genuine-conviction buy against a backdrop of plan-based executive selling elsewhere in the sector. With silver whipsawing in the high-$50s to low-$60s, the lack of sizable open-market buying suggests insiders see fair-to-full value rather than a fresh entry point after the multi-quarter run. No newer Coeur Form 4 has surfaced in the past two weeks, so this remains the latest available.

insiders.rationale: DBS CEO Tan Su Shan sold 100,000 shares at S$60.12 on 15 May 2026, leaving ~1.3 million shares (0.048% of the bank), a partial profit-taking trim shortly after the stock first pushed above S$60 — the most recent verified insider move on the SGX-listed holdings (latest available).
insiders.deepDive: The sale came days after DBS reported 1Q2026 net profit of S$2.93 billion (up 1% y/y, 24% q/q) and as the stock hit record territory; DBS has since pushed to a fresh ~S$67 all-time high into its 6 August results. As Singapore's largest lender's first female CEO, Tan retains a sizeable 1.3 million-share holding, so this is a liquidity/diversification trim rather than a loss of confidence. CEO sells into all-time highs are common and often tax-driven, but can cap near-term sentiment given DBS's elevated ~2.2x book valuation and NIM sensitivity to falling SORA. No within-window (24 June-8 July) substantial-shareholder or director-interest change was verifiable for the SGX holdings this run; DBS continues a S$3bn buyback through 2027.
